decisions.reason: As a relatively generic add-on web service with weaker strategic differentiation than the firm's core regulated-energy data products, it is more likely to fall below aspiration levels and be discontinued so resources can be shifted to the platform business.

This database is close to the firm's core data and compliance capabilities, and with the firm expanding and having some slack it would usually keep such an adjacent niche offer unless results clearly disappoint.
The service fits the firm's established role in helping energy customers handle complex operational and regulatory tasks, so management would likely tolerate some uncertainty and retain it.
A tariff database product line with several models strongly leverages the firm's database assets and platform direction, making it likely to stay unless performance is well below aspirations.
Custom web services support the firm's move toward broader end-to-end digital service provision, so behavioral-theory logic and available slack favor continuation.

Like other generic lookup utilities, this service appears less central to the firm's differentiated energy-market offering and is therefore a plausible candidate to be dropped if its standalone results are mediocre.
